taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Egwi, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 295.88 | 0.54518 | 0.54518
2 | 798.6 | 3.5924 | 4.1376
3 | 864.62 | 2.1559 | 6.2935
4 | 1810.2 | 37.957 | 37.25
5 | 5634.2 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HAA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Egwi, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station: Egwi, Etche LGA.

The VES profile for this station indicates a five-layer sequence with consistently increasing resistivity values: Layer 1 (295.88 ohm-m), Layer 2 (798.6 ohm-m), Layer 3 (864.62 ohm-m), Layer 4 (1810.2 ohm-m), and Layer 5 (5634.2 ohm-m).

Since each consecutive group of three layers follows an increasing resistivity trend ($r_1 < r_2 < r_3$), the correct curve type is 'A'. The current file classification of 'HAA-type' is incorrect, as the resistivity values do not show the initial decrease (where $r_1 > r_2 < r_3$) required to satisfy the 'H' designation for the first group of layers.

{"curve_type_stated": "HAA", "label_issue_flagged": true}
